scope: offline only; no COM, no RF, no flash, no HEX, no cryptography, no keys

design_correction.what_was_wrong: the first RADIOV10 draft let the host supply PAN, short and IEEE for each context as arbitrary values
design_correction.why_that_was_wrong: every predecessor pinned its single context in file-scope constants on purpose. ctx1_rx_admission_v25/src/rejoin_transport.c carries ctx1's RAW and trust-centre addresses, short 0x6c55, epoch id and attempt id as literals, and the V7 and V22 sources before it pinned ctx0 and explicitly refused ctx1. The effect is a safety property: the image cannot address a network it was not built for.
design_correction.correction: a two-entry table of compile-time constants in include/dual_identity.h. The host chooses whether a context is enabled, when it is bound and when it may ACK, and reports the current short; it never chooses which network a context is.
design_correction.short_exception: the coordinator assigns our short and a rejoin can change it, so any plausible short is accepted (not 0x0000, below 0xfff8) rather than only the recorded one

latent_test_defect_found.what: the extended-address test vectors were written in the order of the hex string rather than wire order
latent_test_defect_found.how_it_hid: both the synthetic frame and the binding used the same wrong order, so comparisons matched and the logic was still exercised correctly
latent_test_defect_found.how_it_surfaced: pinning the identities against the firmware's wire-order constants made the mismatch fail immediately
latent_test_defect_found.convention: IEEE addresses are stored and compared least significant byte first, matching ctx1_rx_admission_v25/src/rejoin_transport.c

pinned_table.secrets: none; all of these already appear in committed sources and published result documents, and no key material is in the header

enforcement_points: dual_config_valid refuses a context whose PAN is not its pinned PAN, whose short is not plausible, or whose declared local IEEE is not its pinned RAW identity
dual_binding_set refuses a binding whose PAN, RAW identity, trust-centre identity or key sequence is not this context's pinned value
the admission predicate then compares frames against that validated binding, so a frame carrying the other network's identity under our own PAN and short is refused on air

equivalence_still_holds.note: re-run after the wire-order correction and after pinning, with the unmodified V25 predicate in the same binary

not_done_yet: the state machines in rejoin_transport.c still pin ctx1 only: PAN literals 0x0b7a in the poll builders and the beacon and application envelope checks, short 0x6c55, epoch and attempt strings, keys.ctx=1
session budgets remain 360 s and 400 polls, enforced at rejoin_transport.c lines 47, 49 and 96
main.c still speaks RADIOV9 with one session and no ctx on RX
